data.name: Lydiora
data.gender_notes: Lydiora is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Lydiora is derived from the Hebrew, Greek, and Latin roots 'Ly' meaning 'loyal', 'Dio' meaning 'god', and 'ora' meaning 'sight' or 'watch'. This name embodies the virtues of loyalty, faith, strength, and compassion. It is a beautiful and meaningful name for a little girl. The name Lydiora carries the meaning “Loyal, Faithful, Strong, Compassionate” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Lydiora usually hope their child will grow to embody loyal, faithful, strong, compassionate and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the faithful watchfulness of God over His people.
data.etymology: Lydiora belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Loyal, Faithful, Strong, Compassionate.”

in_greek.name: Λυδίωρα
in_greek.meaning: Λυδίωρα σημαίνει πολύτιμη γυναίκα από τον Θεό
in_greek.long_meaning: Λυδίωρα είναι ένα σπάνιο και ενδιαφέρον όνομα που προέρχεται από την ελληνική γλώσσα και σημαίνει 'πολύτιμη γυναίκα από τον Θεό' ή 'σπάνια και πολύτιμη'. Το όνομα αποτελείται από δύο λέξεις: 'Λυδία' που σημαίνει 'όμορφη γυναίκα' και 'δωρα' που σημαίνει 'δώρο'. Επομένως, το όνομα Λυδίωρα μπορεί να ερμηνευτεί ως 'όμορφο δώρο από τον Θεό' ή 'πολύτιμη και σπάνια γυναίκα'.

in_latin.name: Lydiora
in_latin.meaning: Lydiora means precious woman from God
in_latin.long_meaning: Lydiora is a rare and fascinating name derived from Greek roots, signifying 'precious woman from God' or 'rare and precious'. The name consists of two elements: 'Lydia', meaning 'beautiful woman', and 'dora', meaning 'gift'. Hence, Lydiora can be interpreted as 'beautiful gift from God' or 'precious and rare woman'. In the context of early Christian tradition, names with such etymology often reflected the values of piety, beauty, and divine favor.

In Greek mythology, the goddess Cybele, who was also worshipped as the Magna Mater (Great Mother), was said to have a temple in Sardes. The name Lydiora may be derived from the name of this temple or the city itself, combining 'Lydian' and 'ora' meaning 'shore' or 'land'.

During the Middle Ages, a female saint named Lydwyna of Schiedam or Liduina was venerated in the Netherlands. According to her hagiography, she was a peasant girl who lived in the 5th century AD and was known for her devotion to the Virgin Mary. The name Lydiora may have been derived from this saint's name, with the addition of the suffix '-ora' meaning 'goddess' or 'shrine' in honor of her dedication to the Virgin Mary.
